title: Implement Queue
contract: Process nonnegative numbers as enqueue operations and −1 as dequeue. Return removed values; removing from empty returns −1.
brute: List<Integer> queue=new ArrayList<>(),out=new ArrayList<>();for(int x:operations){if(x>=0)queue.add(x);else out.add(queue.isEmpty()?-1:queue.remove(0));emit("Array-list removal shifts the remaining elements","queue",queue,"removed",out);}return out;
optimal: Deque<Integer> in=new ArrayDeque<>(),outStack=new ArrayDeque<>();List<Integer> out=new ArrayList<>();for(int x:operations){if(x>=0)in.push(x);else{if(outStack.isEmpty())while(!in.isEmpty())outStack.push(in.pop());out.add(outStack.isEmpty()?-1:outStack.pop());}emit("Transfer only when the output stack is empty","input stack",in,"output stack",outStack,"removed",out);}return out;
reasoning: An array-list FIFO is correct but removing index zero shifts every remaining item.
Two stacks reverse the insertion order exactly once when the dequeue stack runs dry.
Each item crosses from input to output at most once, giving amortized constant time per operation; an individual transfer can still cost O(n).
